work_items.title: notification_outbox + notification_log entities (ITenantEntity, FleetId-scoped) + FleetSettings.SmsMonthlyCapCzk/SmsUnitCostCzk + dedup unique index + one migration
work_items.goal: The single serialized Lane-A migration WI (UC-006 precedent: one coherent snapshot, all other Lane-A WIs depend on it). Add TWO new entities: NotificationOutbox (Id, FleetId, Event[enum], OrderId?, Channel[Sms|Push], RecipientUserId?, RecipientPhone?, RecipientEndpoint?, PayloadJson[jsonb], Attempts[int default 0], NextAttemptAt, Status[Queued|Sent|Failed|Skipped], CreatedAt) and NotificationLog (Id, FleetId, Event[enum], OrderId?, Channel, Recipient[string], Status[Queued|Sent|Failed|SkippedCap|SkippedNoChannel], ProviderMessageId?, Error?, CreatedAt, SentAt?). Both implement ITenantEntity (FleetId non-null, tenant-scoped via global query filter, mirroring Order). The DEDUP unique index (AC#7) lives on NotificationLog over (FleetId, Event, OrderId, Recipient, Channel). Add NotificationEvent + NotificationChannel + NotificationStatus enums under Infrastructure/Entities. Add FleetSettings.SmsMonthlyCapCzk (int, default 500) + SmsUnitCostCzk (int, default 1) via the SAME migration. Register both DbSets. PushSubscription already exists in the snapshot (verified InitialSchema) so NO push_subscription migration. Add global query filters for the two new tenant entities in TaxiDbContext.OnModelCreating. One migration AddNotificationTablesAndSmsCap via dotnet ef --output-dir Infrastructure/Migrations. No engine/endpoint logic here - schema only, so the snapshot lands cleanly before the parallel A2..A6 work.
acceptance_criteria: NotificationOutbox and NotificationLog both implement ITenantEntity (non-null FleetId); each gets a global query filter `e => e.FleetId == currentTenant.FleetId` in TaxiDbContext.OnModelCreating alongside the existing Order filter. DbSet<NotificationOutbox> and DbSet<NotificationLog> are registered. Enums (NotificationEvent: OrderCreatedForCustomer, DriverAssigned, DriverArrived, RideStarted, RideCompleted, OrderCancelledByFleet, OrderCancelledByCustomer, OfferToDriver, DriverDeclined, DriverTimedOut, NewAppOrderForDispatch, ScheduledOrderReminder; NotificationChannel: Sms, Push; NotificationStatus: Queued, Sent, Failed, SkippedCap, SkippedNoChannel) are stored as strings (global Enum convention already present).

A UNIQUE index on NotificationLog (FleetId, Event, OrderId, Recipient, Channel) enforces dedup (AC#7). PayloadJson on NotificationOutbox is jsonb (System.Text.Json.JsonDocument? mapped with HasColumnType('jsonb'), CLAUDE.md). FleetId and (Status, NextAttemptAt) on NotificationOutbox are indexed for the dispatch-job scan.

FleetSettings gains SmsMonthlyCapCzk (int, default 500) and SmsUnitCostCzk (int, default 1); FleetSettingsConfiguration sets both defaults via HasDefaultValue so existing rows backfill. A single migration AddNotificationTablesAndSmsCap is added with --output-dir Infrastructure/Migrations (CLAUDE.md); its up-SQL creates two tables + the unique dedup index + adds two non-null columns with defaults, and is reviewed for non-destructive ops (rules/ef-core.md#migrations).

NotificationSchema_OutboxAndLog_AreTenantScoped (fleet A cannot read fleet B's outbox/log rows - tenant isolation), NotificationSchema_DedupIndex_RejectsDuplicateLogRow (inserting a second NotificationLog with the same FleetId+Event+OrderId+Recipient+Channel throws a 23505 PostgresException), and NotificationSchema_FleetSettingsCapDefaults_Are500And1 pass.

work_items.title: POST/DELETE /api/v1/push/subscriptions (all authenticated roles, multi-device, UserId-scoped, upsert + prune)
work_items.goal: Resolve the UC-004 push-subscription-server deferral. Vertical-slice endpoints under Features/Push over the EXISTING PushSubscription entity (verified: Id, FleetId?, UserId, Endpoint, P256dh, Auth, UserAgent?, CreatedAt, LastUsedAt?; UserId-scoped, NOT ITenantEntity, nullable FleetId - mirrors RefreshToken; query filter already admits null FleetId). POST push/subscriptions upserts by (UserId, Endpoint) so re-subscribing the same browser is idempotent and one user may register several devices; it stamps FleetId from the JWT fleet_id claim when present (null for Customer). DELETE push/subscriptions removes by Endpoint for the calling user. Allowed for ANY authenticated role (Customer/Driver/Dispatcher/FleetAdmin). NOTE: there is no existing 'any authenticated' policy (verified policies: CustomerOnly, DriverOnly, DispatcherOnly, FleetAdminOnly, SuperAdminOnly, DispatcherOrCustomer, DispatcherOrDriver, CustomerOrStaff). Add an AuthenticatedOnly policy (RequireAuthenticatedUser) to AuthorizationPolicies and use it here, OR reuse CustomerOrStaff if it already covers all roles - pick the one that admits every role and document the choice. Reads/writes are UserId-scoped (the caller's sub claim), never cross-user. No new migration (PushSubscription already in the snapshot).
acceptance_criteria: POST push/subscriptions accepts { endpoint, p256dh, auth, userAgent? }; a validator requires endpoint/p256dh/auth non-empty (missing field -> 400 with a stable error code, NOT 500 - use plain properties + NotEmpty per the CLAUDE.md 'required on STJ-deserialized request properties' trap). The endpoint upserts by (UserId from the sub claim, Endpoint): a second POST with the same endpoint updates P256dh/Auth/UserAgent/LastUsedAt in place rather than inserting a duplicate. FleetId is stamped from the fleet_id JWT claim when present, left null for Customer. Returns 200/204.

DELETE push/subscriptions accepts { endpoint } and removes the calling user's subscription with that endpoint; a non-existent endpoint is a no-op 204 (idempotent, no 404 leak). Both endpoints require authentication for ALL roles via the chosen all-roles policy (new AuthenticatedOnly or an existing all-role policy); an anonymous request is 401.

A user may hold multiple subscriptions (different endpoints = different devices); subscriptions are UserId-scoped so one user never sees or deletes another user's subscription. Timestamps use the injected TimeProvider (CreatedAt on insert, LastUsedAt left for the push sender to bump).

PushSubscribe_NewEndpoint_Inserts, PushSubscribe_SameEndpointTwice_Upserts (no duplicate row), PushSubscribe_MultipleDevices_AllPersist, PushSubscribe_MissingEndpoint_Returns400, PushUnsubscribe_RemovesOwnEndpoint, PushUnsubscribe_Unknown_Returns204NoLeak, PushSubscribe_Anonymous_Returns401, and PushSubscribe_CustomerAndDriver_BothAllowed pass.

work_items.title: Pure routing matrix (Source + has-push) + GSM-7 Czech templates (build-time <=160 test, AC#5) + dedup-key helper - all unit-tested, no DbContext
work_items.goal: The pure, testable core (no DbContext, no IO) that the engine (A4) and dispatch job (A5) share. THREE pure pieces under Common/Notifications: (1) NotificationRouting.Resolve(NotificationEvent evt, OrderSource source, bool customerHasPush) -> a list of (Recipient role, NotificationChannel) resolved from a STATIC in-code matrix exactly matching assignment section 1: Push preferred, SMS only when the matrix says so; PHONE orders (Source=Phone) get the SMS subset (OrderCreatedForCustomer + DriverArrived only); App+push -> push only; App+no-push -> SMS per the matrix (DriverArrived is SMS-ALWAYS regardless of push, AC#2; RideStarted/RideCompleted are push-only, AC#2). Model it so a per-fleet override is trivial later but DO NOT build the override. (2) SmsTemplates: Czech GSM-7 (no diacritics) render functions for OrderCreated ('Taxi {fleet}: objednavka {code} prijata. Sledujte: {link}') and DriverArrived ('Taxi {fleet}: ridic {driver} je na miste, {plate} {color}.'), plus push title/body templates (DriverAssigned push MAY use diacritics). A GsmSevenValidator.IsGsm7AndWithinLimit(string) -> bool checks every char is in the GSM-7 basic+extension set AND rendered length <= 160. (3) NotificationDedupKey.For(evt, orderId, recipient, channel) -> the canonical string used for the NotificationLog dedup. All three are stateless static/pure classes. TEST-CLASS NAMING: the GSM-7 build-time test class MUST be named NotificationSmsTemplateTests (NOT SmsTemplateGsm7Tests) so its FQN contains the substring 'Notifications.Notification' and is caught by this WI's single-token verification filter - a class named SmsTemplateGsm7Tests would NOT match and the AC#5 build-time test would silently not run in the gate.
acceptance_criteria: NotificationRouting.Resolve returns the correct (recipient, channel) set for every NotificationEvent from the static matrix. Key cases asserted: DriverArrived -> customer gets BOTH push AND SMS (SMS always, AC#2) when a push subscription exists; RideStarted -> customer gets push ONLY (no SMS, AC#2); RideCompleted -> push only; Phone-source order -> customer gets SMS for OrderCreatedForCustomer and DriverArrived ONLY, and nothing for RideStarted/RideCompleted; App+no-push -> OrderCreatedForCustomer resolves to SMS (tracking link); OfferToDriver -> driver push; DriverDeclined/DriverTimedOut/NewAppOrderForDispatch/OrderCancelledByCustomer -> dispatcher push. The matrix is a static table with no DbContext/IO.

GsmSevenValidator.IsGsm7AndWithinLimit returns true for a rendered SMS of valid GSM-7 chars <=160 and false for a diacritic char or >160 chars. SmsTemplates renders OrderCreated and DriverArrived with placeholder substitution ({fleet},{code},{link} / {fleet},{driver},{plate},{color}).

AC#5 build-time test SmsTemplateGsm7Tests renders EVERY SMS template with the LONGEST realistic values (a 30-char fleet name, a 6-char public code, a realistic absolute tracking URL, a long driver name + plate + color) and asserts each rendered message IsGsm7AndWithinLimit (GSM-7 and <=160). This fails the build if any template can exceed 160 GSM-7 chars.
NotificationDedupKey.For is deterministic and identical for the same (evt, orderId, recipient, channel) and differs when any component differs.

NotificationRouting_DriverArrived_SmsEvenWithPush, NotificationRouting_RideStarted_PushOnly, NotificationRouting_PhoneOrder_OnlyCreatedAndArrivedSms, NotificationRouting_AppNoPush_CreatedIsSms, SmsTemplates_AllTemplates_Fit160Gsm7WithLongestValues, SmsTemplates_DiacriticInput_FailsGsm7, and NotificationDedupKey_SameInputs_SameKey pass.

work_items.title: INotificationService.Notify enqueues notification_outbox rows in the SAME DbContext/transaction (AC#3) - wired into OrderService.TransitionAsync (pre-commit) AND CreateOrderEndpoint + pure monthly cost-cap counter (AC#6)
work_items.goal: The load-bearing transactional-outbox core (AC#3). INotificationService.Notify(NotificationEvent evt, Order order, CancellationToken ct) resolves recipients via A3 NotificationRouting (loading the customer's push-subscription presence + applying the monthly cap), renders payloads via A3 templates, and ADDS NotificationOutbox rows to the SAME scoped TaxiDbContext change-tracker - it does NOT call SaveChanges and does NOT open its own scope/context. Atomicity comes from the caller's existing single SaveChangesAsync. CRITICAL CALL-SITES (both verified): (1) OrderService.TransitionAsync - inject INotificationService and call Notify AFTER OrderStateMachine.Apply succeeds and events are added but BEFORE the `await dbContext.SaveChangesAsync(ct)` at line 68 (NOT in the post-commit publish block at lines 77-95 where OrderChanged/NewOrderOffered fire); the outbox rows then commit atomically with the order + order_events. Map the transition result to the event(s): Assign/Reassign -> OfferToDriver; Accept -> DriverAssigned; Arrive -> DriverArrived; Start -> RideStarted; Complete -> RideCompleted; Cancel -> OrderCancelledByFleet/ByCustomer (by actor role); Decline -> DriverDeclined; Timeout -> DriverTimedOut. (2) CreateOrderEndpoint - inject INotificationService and call Notify(OrderCreatedForCustomer or NewAppOrderForDispatch) BEFORE the SaveChangesAsync inside the public-code retry loop (line 206) so the outbox row shares the create transaction; the re-save on a public-code collision re-saves the already-tracked outbox rows harmlessly. PURE cost-cap: NotificationCostCap.Decide(int sentThisMonthCzk, int capCzk, int unitCostCzk, NotificationEvent evt, NotificationChannel channel) -> Allow | SkipCap (100% reached AND not DriverArrived -> SkipCap; DriverArrived always Allow, AC#6; 90% -> a FleetAdmin warning flag). The engine reads the current-month SMS count from notification_log (SentAt within the TimeProvider month window) to feed the pure cap. Do NOT re-price or mutate the order.
acceptance_criteria: INotificationService.Notify ADDS NotificationOutbox rows to the injected scoped TaxiDbContext (the same instance the caller uses) WITHOUT calling SaveChangesAsync and WITHOUT opening a new scope. AC#3: NotificationOutbox_WrittenInSameTransaction proves atomicity - simulate a failure of the caller's SaveChanges (e.g. a concurrency conflict or forced rollback) after Notify and assert NO outbox row is persisted; on success the outbox row and the order/order_events commit together. The outbox insert is BEFORE OrderService line 68 and BEFORE CreateOrderEndpoint line 206, never in the post-commit SignalR publish block.

Notify resolves recipients via A3 NotificationRouting keyed on (event, Order.Source, customerHasPush) where customerHasPush is computed from PushSubscriptions for Order.CustomerUserId. Each outbox row stores INTENT (Event, OrderId, Channel, RecipientUserId?/RecipientPhone?/RecipientEndpoint?) - it does NOT store a pre-rendered SMS body. The SMS body (with the absolute tracking link) is rendered at SEND time by the dispatch job (A5) from the order's then-final PublicCode; this avoids the CreateOrderEndpoint public-code RETRY LOOP (lines 202-216) regenerating PublicCode AFTER a body was already rendered (AC#1 'working tracking link' would otherwise embed a stale code on a rare 23505 collision). The absolute link is built in A5 via TrackingTokenService.Mint(order.Id, now + lifetime) + a new dev-config PublicBaseUrl (added to appsettings.Development.json + an options type here in A4; prod wiring deferred to 08, documented).

CreateOrderRequest gains an additive `OrderSource? Source` (plain property, no `required`); CreateOrderEndpoint sets Source = isCustomer ? App : (req.Source ?? Dispatcher) so a dispatcher can create a Phone-source order. A Phone-source order enqueues exactly ONE OrderCreatedForCustomer SMS outbox row (AC#1).

Dedup (AC#7) - enforcement lives at SEND time in A5, NOT at enqueue: the outbox may contain two rows for the same (event,order,recipient,channel) after a duplicate Notify, and that is fine; the dispatch job (A5) CLAIMS the NotificationLog row via the unique-index insert (claim-then-execute, the existing IdempotencyRecord pattern) BEFORE calling the sender, so a 23505 means 'already sent/claimed' -> skip the send entirely. A4 therefore does NOT attempt to dedup at enqueue; it only ensures Notify enqueues outbox intent. A4's NotificationDedup_DuplicateNotify_EnqueuesButSendGuardedByA5 documents the hand-off (the send-once assertion itself is A5's NotificationDispatchJob_DuplicateOutbox_InvokesSenderOnce).

PURE NotificationCostCap.Decide (AC#6): with cap=2 and unit cost=1, after 2 SMS already sent this month a third NON-arrival SMS decides SkipCap (logged SkippedCap, no send) while a DriverArrived SMS decides Allow (still sends). NotificationCostCap_ThirdNonArrival_SkipsCap, NotificationCostCap_ArrivalAlwaysAllowed, and NotificationCostCap_At90Percent_FlagsWarning pass (pure unit tests, no DB).

Tenant safety: outbox/log rows carry the order's FleetId and are written through the tenant-scoped context. NotificationOutbox_IsWrittenForCorrectFleet (an order in fleet A never enqueues an outbox row readable by fleet B) passes. No raw phone numbers or tokens are logged (rules/logging.md) - use Reason/Phase discriminators and OrderId/FleetId.

work_items.title: ISmsSender (Console/GoSms/SMSbrana, config-selected) + IPushSender (WebPush 1.0.13 VAPID, 410->delete, AC#4) + NotificationDispatchJob RunTickAsync shell (retry 3x, AC#1/#3) + notification_log writes
work_items.goal: The channel adapters + the background drain job (mirrors OfferTimeoutJob's RunTickAsync testable-shell, CLAUDE.md WI-14). CHANNELS: ISmsSender with ConsoleSmsSender (DEFAULT in dev/test - writes the message via the injected logger so AC#1 can assert it; the <=80-line GoSmsSender (HTTP) and SMSbranaSmsSender behind config are ALSO written but untested against live API, config selects one via a Notifications:SmsProvider setting). IPushSender using WebPush 1.0.13 (author coryjthompson, the web-push-csharp lib; targets netstandard2.1/net8.0, compatible with .NET 10; VAPID via VapidDetails; 410 detected via WebPushException.StatusCode == Gone) with a NoOpPushSender for tests; payload <=3KB { title, body, url, tag, priority }; on HttpStatusCode.Gone (410) the sender DELETES the matching PushSubscription (AC#4). VAPID keys are dev-config only (appsettings.Development.json; prod -> 08, documented). JOB: NotificationDispatchJob : BackgroundService with a thin ExecuteAsync PeriodicTimer shell and all logic in public RunTickAsync(ct) (tests call it directly, no timer waits). Per tick: scan NotificationOutbox cross-tenant (IgnoreQueryFilters) for Status=Queued/Failed-retryable with NextAttemptAt<=now; per row open a FRESH scope, set CurrentTenant.FleetId = row.FleetId (so notification_log writes pass the tenant guard + query filter). AC#7 SEND-ONCE via CLAIM-THEN-EXECUTE (the existing IdempotencyRecord pattern): INSERT the NotificationLog row (Status=Queued) FIRST as a claim - if the unique dedup index rejects it (23505), another outbox row already claimed this (event,order,recipient,channel) so SKIP the send entirely (no second sender call); only on a successful claim does the job call the channel sender. RENDER AT SEND TIME: the SMS body (OrderCreated absolute tracking link) is rendered here from the order's then-final PublicCode via A3 SmsTemplates + TrackingTokenService.Mint + PublicBaseUrl - NOT at enqueue (avoids the CreateOrder public-code retry-loop staleness). RETRY COMPATIBILITY INVARIANT: a row's OWN failed send must stay retryable - the claim is keyed so a row can re-attempt its own send (match the claim to the outbox row / keep the log row non-terminal until Sent), while a DIFFERENT duplicate outbox row is blocked. After the send, update the claimed log row to Sent (+ProviderMessageId/SentAt) or on failure bump Attempts + NextAttemptAt (backoff via TimeProvider); after 3 failed attempts mark the outbox row + the log row Status=Failed. Register the job in JobsServiceExtensions.AddJobs.
acceptance_criteria: ISmsSender has ConsoleSmsSender (default, logs the rendered message so tests assert it), GoSmsSender (HTTP, <80 lines), and SmsbranaSmsSender, selected by Notifications:SmsProvider config (default Console in dev/test). IPushSender has WebPushSender (WebPush 1.0.13, VAPID from dev-config NotificationOptions; prod keys -> 08 documented) and NoOpPushSender (tests). The WebPush package reference is added to Taxi.Api.csproj at the pinned version 1.0.13.

NotificationDispatchJob mirrors OfferTimeoutJob: a thin ExecuteAsync PeriodicTimer(timeProvider) shell + a public RunTickAsync(ct) with all logic; tests construct the job and call RunTickAsync directly (no timer waits, CLAUDE.md WI-14). The scan uses IgnoreQueryFilters cross-tenant; each row is dispatched in a fresh scope with CurrentTenant.FleetId set from the row before writing notification_log. Registered via AddJobs.

AC#1: PhoneOrderSmsEndToEnd creates a Phone-source order (A4 Source field), runs RunTickAsync once with ConsoleSmsSender, and asserts EXACTLY ONE SMS was produced, its body contains a working ABSOLUTE tracking link, and a single NotificationLog row Status=Sent exists (ConsoleSmsSender output asserted).

AC#3: NotificationDispatchJob_SendFailsThreeTimes_MarksFailed - with a sender stubbed to throw, after 3 RunTickAsync passes the outbox row + the NotificationLog are Status=Failed (and the dispatcher board red icon surfaces via the A6 Notifikace list carrying a Failed SMS). Backoff uses TimeProvider; the test advances its own FakeTime (own factory per the CLAUDE.md TaxiApiFactory.FakeTime note).

AC#4: PushSender_Returns410_DeletesSubscription - a push send whose provider returns 410 Gone causes the matching PushSubscription row to be deleted. AC#7: NotificationDispatchJob_DuplicateOutbox_InvokesSenderOnce - with a RECORDING sender, two outbox rows for the same (event,order,recipient,channel) result in the sender being invoked EXACTLY ONCE (the claim-then-execute NotificationLog insert rejects the second BEFORE its send) and exactly one Sent log row. This asserts the SEND boundary (not just the log count) - the claim happens before the sender call.

notification_log and outbox are written tenant-scoped; a dispatch for fleet A never writes a log row visible to fleet B (tenant isolation). No raw phone/token/VAPID key is logged - only Reason/Phase/OrderId/FleetId/ProviderMessageId (rules/logging.md).

work_items.title: OrderDetailDto gains an additive notifications list (sent/failed) + GetOrderEndpoint projection so the dispatcher sees delivery status (AC#3 red icon source)
work_items.goal: Close the visibility gap (assignment section 5). OrderDetailDto/OrderDetailMapper gains an additive `notifications` list (each item: { event, channel, recipient, status, error?, createdAt, sentAt? }) projected from NotificationLog for the order. GetOrderEndpoint (and the shared OrderDetailMapper used by CreateOrder/transition detail responses) populates it - load the NotificationLog rows for the order with AsNoTracking (tenant-scoped) and map in memory (no jsonb in the projection). This is the server half of the dispatcher 'Notifikace' section + the failed-SMS red-icon signal (a Failed Sms log row = the red icon). Additive only: existing OrderDetailDto fields, callers, and the { order } envelope are unchanged. No state-machine change, no new migration.
acceptance_criteria: OrderDetailDto gains an additive `notifications` array (OrderNotificationDto record: Event, Channel, Recipient, Status, Error?, CreatedAt, SentAt?). OrderDetailMapper/GetOrderEndpoint populate it from NotificationLog rows for the order (AsNoTracking, tenant-scoped, ordered by CreatedAt). Existing fields + the { order } envelope are unchanged (purely additive).

A completed order whose customer SMS went to Status=Failed surfaces that Failed Sms item in `notifications` so the dispatcher UI (B2) can render the red icon and call the customer (AC#3 server half). A Sent item shows SentAt.
Tenant isolation: GetOrder for an order in fleet A only returns fleet A notification rows; a cross-fleet order id is a no-leak 404 (existing behavior unchanged).
OrderDetail_IncludesSentAndFailedNotifications and OrderDetail_NotificationsAreTenantScoped pass.

work_items.title: Service-worker push display + click-to-open url + subscription wiring to A2 (driver mandatory, customer after first order) + client.ts subscribe/unsubscribe
work_items.goal: The PWA push half (resolves UC-003 driver-priming + UC-004 customer-prompt deferrals on the client side). The /web service worker shows the push notification ({ title, body, url, tag, priority }) and on notificationclick opens/focuses `url`; OfferToDriver uses requireInteraction:true + the driver app sound (reuse UC-003 offer sound infra). Add pushSubscribe/pushUnsubscribe to client.ts POSTing/DELETEing /push/subscriptions with the browser PushSubscription JSON (endpoint, keys.p256dh, keys.auth, userAgent). Wire the subscription lifecycle: a pure subscription-manager module (request permission, subscribe via the VAPID public key from config, POST to the API) called for the DRIVER mandatorily at login (UC-003 PermissionPriming) and for the CUSTOMER after the first order (UC-004 PushPrompt, already present - wire its accept to pushSubscribe). VAPID public key is a dev build-config value (prod -> 08). Pure logic (payload->display mapping, subscription-manager decisioning) extracted and unit-tested; SW + browser Push API are thin shells.
acceptance_criteria: client.ts gains pushSubscribe({ endpoint, p256dh, auth, userAgent }) -> POST /push/subscriptions and pushUnsubscribe(endpoint) -> DELETE /push/subscriptions, both via the typed client (no raw fetch), attaching the X-Fleet-Slug/JWT as the existing client does. Responses are unwrapped per the client.ts named-envelope convention.

The service worker push handler renders a notification from the { title, body, url, tag, priority } payload; notificationclick opens or focuses `url`. For a payload with priority high / tag offer it sets requireInteraction:true and triggers the driver sound. pushPayload.ts (pure) maps a raw push payload to the display options and is unit-tested (including the OfferToDriver requireInteraction branch).

pushSubscriptionManager.ts (pure) decides subscribe/skip from (permission state, existing subscription, role) and builds the API request from a browser PushSubscription; it is unit-tested with mocked permission/subscription. The driver login path subscribes mandatorily (UC-003 priming) and the customer PushPrompt accept calls pushSubscribe (UC-004). No /x, /d, or /c route owned by another group is modified beyond the shared push module + the customer PushPrompt.

npm run tsc, npm run lint (--max-warnings 0), npm run test pass; pushPayload.test.ts, pushSubscriptionManager.test.ts, usePushSubscription.test.ts (client mocked per rules/web-testing.md#network-mocking), and locales.parity.test.ts pass. New i18n keys land in both cs.json + en.json (formal 'vy' for customer, informal 'ty' for driver).

work_items.title: Dispatcher order-detail 'Notifikace' section (sent/failed) + failed-SMS red icon on the order card + SMS cap/cost in settings
work_items.goal: The dispatcher visibility half. In the /x order-detail view render a 'Notifikace' section listing the A6 `notifications` items (event, channel, recipient, status, time) with a clear sent/failed visual; a FAILED Sms item shows a red icon on the order card (so the dispatcher calls the customer). Add the monthly SMS count + estimated cost + cap-warning to the dispatcher Settings (reuse the FleetSettings surface; the cap numbers come from FleetSettings.SmsMonthlyCapCzk/SmsUnitCostCzk + the current-month count - a read-only display). Pure status->pill/icon mapping extracted and tested. Component-tested (+axe); no new e2e (the create-order/accept/customer flows are already e2e-covered and this is a display addition).
acceptance_criteria: The order-detail view renders a 'Notifikace' section listing each notification (translated event label, channel, recipient, status, time formatted Europe/Prague) from the A6 order DTO `notifications` field; the DTO type in client.ts is extended additively. A Failed Sms item renders with a clear failed state (role/aria, not color alone).

OrderCard shows a red icon (with an i18n'd aria-label, e.g. 'SMS se nepodarila odeslat') when the order has at least one Failed Sms notification, so the dispatcher knows to call the customer. notificationStatus.ts (pure) maps a status to its pill/icon descriptor and is unit-tested (Sent/Failed/Queued/SkippedCap).

Dispatcher Settings shows the current-month SMS count + estimated cost (count * SmsUnitCostCzk, Intl.NumberFormat cs-CZ) and a cap warning when near/over SmsMonthlyCapCzk (read-only display). Touch targets >= 48px; new i18n keys in both cs.json + en.json; the change does not modify /d or /c routes.

npm run tsc, npm run lint (--max-warnings 0), npm run test pass; notificationStatus.test.ts, a NotificationsSection render + axe assertion, an OrderCard red-icon test, and locales.parity.test.ts pass.

notes: UC-005 = 6 Lane A (api) WIs (A1..A6) + 2 Lane B (web) WIs (B1,B2) = 8 total. Array is topologically ordered and acyclic. Schema shape matches the operative UC-006 handoff (per-WI: id, lane [api|web], title, goal, depends_on, estimated_complexity XS/S/M/L/XL, files_touched, rule_citations, required_reads, needs_library_research, acceptance_criteria, verification {tool, filter}). verification.tool enum used: dotnet-test | vitest; dotnet-test filter is a single-token FullyQualifiedName~Taxi.Api.Tests.Notifications[.<Area>] fragment. NO .claude/schemas/work-items.v1.json file exists (known scaffold gap, CLAUDE.md); this matches the UC-002/003/004/006 handoff shape the conductor consumes. ============ TRANSACTIONAL OUTBOX CALL-SITE (AC#3, load-bearing, SOURCE-VERIFIED): OrderService.TransitionAsync commits at the SINGLE `await dbContext.SaveChangesAsync(ct)` on line 68; it publishes OrderChanged/DriverStatusChanged/NewOrderOffered POST-COMMIT at lines 77-95. The notification_outbox insert MUST go BEFORE line 68 (after OrderStateMachine.Apply succeeds + dbContext.OrderEvents.AddRange(result.Events) at line 61, before order.Version++/SaveChanges), NOT in the post-commit publish block. Mechanism: INotificationService injects the SAME scoped TaxiDbContext and only ADDS outbox rows to the change-tracker (no SaveChanges, no new scope) so order + order_events + outbox commit in one implicit transaction. CreateOrderEndpoint is the SECOND call-site (OrderCreatedForCustomer / NewAppOrderForDispatch): it commits at the SaveChangesAsync inside the public-code retry loop (line 206) - Notify is called BEFORE that loop-save, and the public-code-collision re-save harmlessly re-persists the already-tracked outbox rows. WORDING RECONCILIATION: the assignment says 'Notify after each COMMITTED transition' but AC#3 says 'same transaction' - resolution: Notify = ENQUEUE the outbox row pre-commit (same tx); the actual SEND happens later in NotificationDispatchJob. Stated so the reviewer does not flag the apparent contradiction. ============ PUSH SUBSCRIPTION RECONCILIATION (SOURCE-VERIFIED): PushSubscription ENTITY already exists (Id, FleetId?, UserId, Endpoint, P256dh, Auth, UserAgent?, CreatedAt, LastUsedAt?) and is in TaxiDbContextModelSnapshot (InitialSchema) with a DbSet + a query filter that admits null FleetId (e => e.FleetId == null || e.FleetId == currentTenant.FleetId) + a SaveChanges guard clause - it is UserId-scoped, NOT ITenantEntity (mirrors RefreshToken), nullable FleetId.
